newsitem.title: USA: Western National sales may top $2 bln--CEO.
newsitem.headline: Western National sales may top $2 bln--CEO.

text.p: Western National Corp Chief Executive Officer Michael Poulos said Wednesday the company expects sales to hit $2 billion and possibly more in 1997.
He also said at the life insurance firm's annual meeting that there was no disagreement with analysts' estimates that Western National will earn around $1.75 a share this year, up from $1.53 in 1996.

"We will come in comfortably with $2 billion (in sales), maybe a tad more," Poulos told Reuters. He said sales in April were $227 million and that May would also be strong, but that the summer months would likely bring a seasonal slowdown.

The company had sales of $1.6 billion in 1996 and $517 million in the first quarter of 1997. Its growth is being propelled by what it calls proprietary annuities sold in partnership with banks. Poulos said "probably 75 percent" of April's sales were those instruments.
Poulos said analysts were predicting earnings of around $123 million, or about $1.75 per share, for 1997.
"We certainly don't have any strong argument with that. We came in the first quarter at $0.41 (a share), which was a record quarter, and we think that should improve going forward."
The Houston-based company, which has $10.7 billion in assets, had a 2.21 percent investment spread in the first quarter.

Asked if that level could be maintained for the year, Poulos said, "We think we're able to meet our target zone of 2.15 to 2.20 percent. The 2.21 is a tad on the high side, but we expect certainly we'll be in that range."
Western National currently sells its proprietary annuities, which are aimed at individuals seeking to save for retirement, in partnership with 10 financial institutions.
Poulos said negotiations were under way with several more potential partners and that "we would expect more announcements (on partnerships) in, say, 90 to 120 days."

Western National is 46 percent owned by insurance giant American General Corp, also Houston-based. Many analysts expect American General to buy the rest of Western National, perhaps sometime this year, but Poulos said nothing was currently in the works.
"There are no discussions. I think that's the key point," he said.
